newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end sharply lower on bank concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end sharply lower on bank concerns.

text.p: Investors sold stocks almost across the board on Tuesday on concerns that bank earnings might drop this year as some major banks cut interest rates, driving the index down 2.07 percent by the close, brokers said.

"Apart from selling bank issues, investors also sold communication stocks after an approval was given by the cabinet to allow new mobile phone operators to enter the market," said Bumnan Liumsuwan of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index dropped 13.89 points to 658.59 on 3.8 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index fell 1.39 points to 48.68.
Decliners led gainers 237 to 68 while 81 issues remained unchanged.

Brokers said although the cut on key lending rates by 25 basis point by three banks, which became effective on Tuesday, was considered small, investors were worried it could set a rate easing trend among banks and affect their earnings later.
The cut in interest rates received mixed reaction from investors.
Brokers said some investors wanted to see more cuts in interest rates in order to help stimulate the slowing economy.
Major banks that cut their minimum lending rates were Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and Krung Thai Bank Plc.
Today's index closing level was the lowest for this year, after a new 1997 low was hit on Monday at 672.48.

All major sectors, except energy, dropped on Tuesday. The banking sector fell most in terms of value, retreating 2.20 percent. The energy sector gained 1.26 percent. Bangkok Bank was most active, down five baht to 173. United Communication fell 12 to 138 and PTT Exploration rose 10 to 318. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
